speaker: Timothy L. Farnes
title: Divine Appointments
summary: President Farnes teaches that covenant followers of Jesus Christ minister with compassion to whoever God places in their path, and that this everyday ministering is how we keep the covenant we renew at the sacrament. He tells of a discouraged day when Elder Dallin H. Oaks stopped him in a temple dressing room to ask how he was really doing, then years later did not remember it and said 'it's what we do,' and of helping a terrified new missionary through an airport. He asks everyone to pray daily for eyes to see these 'divine appointments' and to put compassion into action.

findings.quote: “Let your covenants guide your actions. When you have a choice to make, remember your covenant relationship with God. Be loyal to Him. Ask yourself: Does this align with my covenants? For example, do I love and minister to others, comfort people who need comfort, and stand as a witness of Christ—everywhere and always?” (For the Strength of Youth, 36).

See Moroni 4:3; Doctrine and Covenants 20:77; For the Strength of Youth, 35. I hope that each Aaronic Priesthood holder can see what an important service they are performing when they administer the sacrament, to help us receive that sacred power in our lives. It is such a simple ordinance, and yet the blessings of that covenant extend indefinitely, to multitudes of God’s children.

detail.who: For the Strength of Youth (with Farnes's own aside)

findings.quote: “Love your neighbor. And who is your neighbor? Everyone! … “… Reach out to those who may feel lonely, isolated, or helpless. Help them feel Heavenly Father’s love through you” (For the Strength of Youth, 29, 30).

“[A] promise connected to baptism and the sacrament is the constant companionship of [the Lord’s] Spirit and the ministering of angels. You never have to face your challenges alone. God never abandons His covenant children—you can count on that” (For the Strength of Youth, 36–37).

“Heavenly Father does not expect you to do this work on your own. He is with you. When you humbly offer your time and heart, He will do amazing things through you. Jesus Christ is your strength!” (For the Strength of Youth, 16).

See Matthew 25:34–40; Mosiah 2:17. Often, during the sacrament, we think about how we did at keeping the commandments during the previous week. That kind of self-reflection can be good. But a covenant doesn’t just look back; it looks forward. It’s not so much about what we’ve done in the past; it’s more about what we’re willing to do in the future—in Christ’s name and with His help. (See Patrick Kearon, “Welcome to the Church of Joy,” Liahona, Nov. 2024, 37.)
findings.ref: Welcome to the Church of Joy
findings.note: Farnes's own aside that the sacrament covenant looks forward, pointing to Elder Patrick Kearon

findings.quote: “Act on spiritual impressions you receive. If you have a thought or impression to do something kind that will bless someone, do it! All good things come from God. Show your Heavenly Father that He can trust you to follow impressions from Him” (For the Strength of Youth, 12).

We often think of compassion as something we feel, but for Christ, it was something He did. Like faith, compassion gets life from our actions (see James 2:17). As President Russell M. Nelson said, “One of the easiest ways to identify a true follower of Jesus Christ is how compassionately that person treats other people” (“Peacemakers Needed,” Liahona, May 2023, 98).
findings.note: Cites President Russell M. Nelson on compassion as the mark of a true follower
